caption: Figure 1: Two-stream architecture for video classification.
description:
Figure type: Diagram
Description: The figure illustrates a two-stream architecture for video classification. It consists of a spatial stream and a temporal stream, both using convolutional neural networks (ConvNets). The spatial stream processes single frames, while the temporal stream processes multi-frame optical flow. Both streams have similar structures with convolutional layers, pooling layers, and fully connected layers, ending with a softmax layer for classification.

caption: Figure 2: Optical flow. (a),(b): a pair of consecutive video frames with the area around a moving hand outlined with a cyan rectangle. (c): a close-up of dense optical flow in the outlined area; (d): horizontal component d x of the displacement vector field (higher intensity corresponds to positive values, lower intensity to negative values). (e): vertical component d y . Note how (d) and (e) highlight the moving hand and bow. The input to a ConvNet contains multiple flows (Sect. 3.1).

caption: Figure 3: ConvNet input derivation from the multi-frame optical flow. Left: optical flow stacking (1) samples the displacement vectors d at the same location in multiple frames. Right: trajectory stacking (2) samples the vectors along the trajectory. The frames and the corresponding displacement vectors are shown with the same colour.
description:
Section 1: Figure type and content description.
This is a conceptual diagram showing two methods for deriving input for a convolutional neural network (ConvNet) from multi-frame optical flow data. The left panel illustrates "optical flow stacking" which samples displacement vectors at the same location across multiple frames. The right panel shows "trajectory stacking" which samples vectors along a trajectory. Both methods use the same color scheme to represent frames and corresponding displacement vectors.

Section 2: Figure details.

The left panel has arrows labeled "d_τ+2(p1)", "d_τ+1(p1)", and "d_τ(p1)" pointing to vectors at point P1. The right panel has arrows labeled "d_τ+2(p3)", "d_τ+1(p2)", and "d_τ(p1)" pointing to vectors at points P1 and P2.

## Description
This figure is a visualization of convolutional filters from a two-stream convolutional network. It shows 96 columns, each representing a filter, and 20 rows, each corresponding to an input channel. The filters are applied to 10 stacked optical flows, with the top half focusing on horizontal flow components and the bottom half on vertical flow components.

description:

The highest accuracy is observed for activities like "Apply Eye Makeup" and "Baby Crawling," while the lowest accuracy is seen for activities like "Writing" and "YOLO."
